title: Delta-Prefill Switching: Adaptive Routing for Speculative Decoding in Multi-Turn LLM Serving

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to find a routing signal that predicts when speculative decoding is beneficial in prefix-cached multi-turn serving. None of the prior papers explicitly address this specific empirical relationship or prediction task. While many papers discuss speculative decoding (e.g., [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [7], [8], [11], [13], [14]), they focus on improving speculative decoding efficiency, scheduling, or throughput, not on identifying a predictive signal for routing decisions in prefix-cached multi-turn serving. No prior paper establishes the same empirical relationship between Delta-L and speculative decoding benefits.

### Mechanism
The mechanism identifies incremental prompt growth (Delta-L) as the routing signal: small Delta-L favors speculation, while large Delta-L makes speculation costly under concurrency. None of the prior papers propose or analyze Delta-L as a routing signal. Papers like [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [7], [8], [11], [13], and [14] discuss speculative decoding mechanisms, but they focus on draft model selection, scheduling, or throughput optimization rather than introducing Delta-L or an equivalent primitive for routing decisions. No paper uses a substantively equivalent mechanism.

### Evaluation
The contribution validates its findings via DPS routing experiments on ToolBench and BFCL benchmarks. Papers like [12] and [18] discuss benchmarks for speculative decoding or multi-step LLM function calling, but they do not use ToolBench or BFCL specifically. However, the evaluation design — routing experiments with benchmarks — is a standard approach in speculative decoding research. Papers such as [1], [3], [4], [7], [8], [11], [12], and [13] use similar evaluation designs (benchmark-based validation of speculative decoding methods). The specific benchmarks (ToolBench and BFCL) are new instances, but the evaluation design itself is covered.

### Domain
The domain is multi-turn LLM serving with speculative decoding. Many prior papers ([1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [7], [8], [11], [13], [14]) work in the same general application area of LLM inference acceleration via speculative decoding. While this contribution targets a specific sub-problem (prefix-cached multi-turn serving), the domain is not genuinely new. It falls within the broader area of speculative decoding for LLM inference.
